description: Prepare an isolated website ledger and runner lane, then import only the supplied website into website/ without altering existing firmware work.
steps: OWNER (2026-11-21, confirmed to the Author): import the website from the owner's export, finish it, add 'See in 3D' (the StickS3 with the Guardian face on its screen ONLY; no 3D head), deploy on Vercel as project m5-guardian. Plan reviewed by Codex gpt-6-astra (high, read-only), verdict REVISE, all its changes adopted in these rows. The source folder path is given to the worker in the run prompt, never written into this public ledger.
Supervisor: verify that the firmware runner and its worker have exited; record the target revision and existing dirty-file list outside the public repository before editing the shared runner.
Supervisor: create website-tasks.json with exactly W01, W02, W03, W05 and W06 in this order, using this schema and passes=false; include no workstation paths, credentials or execution receipts.

Supervisor: add validated RALPH_LEDGER selection to tools/ralph_runner.py, defaulting to guardian-tasks.json; preserve the firmware data directory and assign website-tasks.json to a separate ralph-website directory.

Supervisor: bind receipt directories to the resolved ledger identity, reject mismatched reuse through RALPH_DATA_ROOT, add a common checkout execution lock, and detect changes to either acceptance ledger during a worker run.

Supervisor: add a website worker prompt naming the selected ledger and website task scope; retain reviewer-owned acceptance and prohibit worker commits, publication, firmware changes and harness edits. Document explicit one-task invocations and supervisor-owned deployment in docs/ralph.md.

Supervisor: add and pass focused runner tests for default and website selection, invalid paths, prompt rendering, receipt isolation, shared-lock exclusion, ledger mutation detection, retry handling and non-batch review boundaries; launch no real worker from these tests.

Copy only the supplied website directory into website/, excluding .git, .vercel, .env files, node_modules, .next, out, caches, logs, browser reports, tsconfig.tsbuildinfo and generated next-env.d.ts; verify that imported source and image bytes match the source before documented corrections.
Extend website/.gitignore for Vercel state and generated test/build artifacts; set Node engines to 24.x, retain pnpm 12.3.4, and make typecheck generate Next types before running tsc --noEmit.

Using Node 24.x and pnpm 12.3.4, complete a frozen-lockfile install, typecheck, the existing six tests and a production build; preserve the lockfile and record actual tool versions and command results outside the public tree.

Run the root public check with the owner's private map required; inspect the exact publication file list and confirm that every pre-existing firmware change is preserved. Limit W01 edits outside website/ to website-tasks.json, runner support, its prompt, focused tests and docs/ralph.md.

description: Finish the English landing page with accurate product wording, complete metadata, clear licensing, readable responsive layouts and accessible controls.
steps: Remove the optional-cigar claim; replace the claim covering every advertised security state with five rated outcomes plus unrated/stale handling; qualify receive-only as monitoring and disclose setup/update transmission and update listening gaps.

Replace traffic inspection with inspection of clients' application traffic; scope no-companion-computer and no-cloud claims to normal monitoring; state that this website is a simulation and does not connect to or protect a visitor's network.

Add a website claim-to-source record covering every factual device statement, with repository-relative source paths and quotations; distinguish current behavior, host-only validation and deferred features, and link the published coverage and limitations documents.

Preserve the reserved-artwork notice, correct its relocated references, record the owner's specified website/screen/social-card use without granting general reuse, and add separate working links for code and artwork licenses.

Make the repository-path row a real link; verify all local anchors and every GitHub file/fragment link against the published branch, retaining synthetic network names and explicitly labeled example counts.

Set metadataBase, canonical URL and Open Graph URL to https://m5-guardian.vercel.app; use a consistent title and description; add a 1200x630 social card with matching metadata while retaining the SVG favicon.

Add app/not-found.tsx with a home link, production robots and sitemap routes, and verify that an unknown URL returns HTTP 404 while the icon, social image, robots and sitemap return successful responses.

Increase essential mobile body text to at least 14px and controls/disclaimers to at least 12px; retain the interface-illustration disclaimer at all breakpoints; fix the identified low-contrast text colors and verify normal text at 4.5:1 or greater.

Add Escape handling and appropriate focus restoration to mobile navigation; forward ToggleGroup orientation to its primitive; retain visible keyboard focus and verify single-selection behavior in both selectors.
Synchronize motion controls with changes to prefers-reduced-motion, reset pointer tilt when motion stops, and suppress decorative hover motion when paused or reduced motion is requested.

Verify all controls and content at widths 320, 375, 390, 600, 768, 1024 and 1440 CSS pixels and at 200 percent zoom; require no horizontal page overflow, clipped controls, obscured text or inaccessible navigation.
Pass typecheck, presentation tests and a production build; record browser keyboard and screen-reader results, including announcements for mood, nearby, alert and stale changes.

description: Add an on-demand rotatable StickS3 viewer with the current Guardian presentation confined to its screen, preserving a functional 2D fallback.
steps: Pin three to 0.186.1, @react-three/fiber to 9.8.1, @react-three/drei to 10.7.9, @types/three to 0.186.0, and react/react-dom together to 19.3.1; retain Next 16.4.6, update the lockfile and verify declared peer compatibility.

Copy only sticks3-front.stl, sticks3-back.stl and sticks3-buttons.stl from the specified reference; verify their SHA-256 values against the inspected source files and record upstream CAD revision/path and conversion provenance.

Add the complete M5Stack MIT notice and model provenance to root THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and a served public/models notice; record the permission and attribution basis for adapting the sibling viewer source.

Add See in 3D and Back to 2D controls to GuardianStage, using its existing Presentation and motion state; keep the 2D view visible until the 3D scene is ready and preserve the selection when switching modes.

Load the viewer through a conditionally mounted client-side dynamic import with SSR disabled; verify from a fresh browser network trace that no Three/Fiber/Drei viewer chunk or STL is requested before activation on desktop or mobile.

Render the Guardian artwork on a correctly oriented screen plane inside the StickS3 bezel; update normal, nearby and alert textures from the current presentation, and clear the previous face for stale data while displaying an explicit no-fresh-data screen.
Support pointer/touch rotation, keyboard arrow rotation and reset, a readable instruction label, visible focus and a 2D return control; keep the current demo status accessible outside the canvas.
Make the existing pause control and prefers-reduced-motion stop automatic rotation and inertial settling; respond to preference changes and suspend unnecessary rendering when the viewer is hidden.

Handle unavailable WebGL, renderer initialization failure, chunk failure, missing STL, failed face image and WebGL context loss with a visible explanation and usable 2D fallback; keep the rest of the page operational.

Clean up textures, derived geometries, environment resources and pointer listeners on replacement or unmount; test toggling back to 2D during an active drag and repeated activation without accumulating listeners or canvases.

Add tests for toggle state preservation, all twenty mood/scenario mappings, stale texture clearing and failure fallback; run production-browser checks with WebGL available and deliberately unavailable.

Verify that the 3D output contains only the StickS3 and its screen artwork, with no standalone Guardian head, Blender export, GLB head mode, Doutor VPD sticker or unrelated product behavior; pass typecheck, tests and production build.

description: Create reproducible website quality gates and verify the complete site in production mode before deployment.
steps: Add a website check script and root make website-check target that run Next type generation, TypeScript checking, all presentation/viewer tests and a production build, returning nonzero on any failure.

Add a website-checks GitHub Actions workflow using Node 24.x and pnpm 12.3.4 with frozen installation and a lockfile-keyed cache; trigger it for website files, the workflow, Makefile, check scripts and product-documentation inputs, plus manual dispatch.

Ensure the test command discovers the new test files rather than executing only lib/guardian.test.ts; run browser checks against the production server and retain failed-check logs and screenshots as CI artifacts.

Run three mobile Lighthouse audits with a pinned Lighthouse version and recorded configuration; require median performance at least 90, accessibility 100, SEO at least 95, LCP at most 2.5 seconds, CLS at most 0.1 and TBT at most 200 milliseconds.

Run automated accessibility checks in normal, nearby, alert, stale, mobile-navigation and active-3D states with no serious or critical findings; complete manual keyboard and screen-reader checks for focus, names, selection, status updates and fallback recovery.

Repeat responsive checks at 320, 375, 390, 600, 768, 1024 and 1440 pixels and 200 percent zoom; verify the disclaimer, license text, navigation and 3D controls remain visible and usable without horizontal page overflow.

Assert that initial loading and waiting without interaction request no 3D chunks or models; after activation, verify model and texture requests succeed and screenshot the screen alignment from front, side and rear views.

Verify response status, metadata, canonical links, social-image dimensions, favicon, robots, sitemap, custom 404 and configured headers from the production build; check browser logs for uncaught errors and hydration failures.

Run the root generic public check in CI and the full private-map check locally; review the exact publication diff and confirm that firmware source, captures, keys, local Vercel state and execution receipts are absent from the website change.
Record evidence against the final reviewed source revision and obtain independent supervisor acceptance of W01, W02, W03 and W05 before production deployment.

description: Deploy the accepted website through the intended Vercel project and verify production behavior and firmware-only build skipping.
steps: Supervisor: verify the intended Vercel account/scope, access to fcavalcantirj/m5-guardian, project-name availability and assignability of m5-guardian.vercel.app; create or select project m5-guardian without inferring availability from an HTTP 404.
Set the Git repository to fcavalcantirj/m5-guardian, production branch to main, framework to Next.js, Root Directory to website and Node version to 24.x; verify these values from project settings.

Configure installation to execute pnpm 12.3.4 with a frozen lockfile and build from website/ using the website quality script; retain Next's framework output handling and verify the actual package-manager version in build logs.

Use the repository root as the source root for any CLI link/deployment, with project Root Directory website; keep .vercel state ignored and verify that the uploaded source resolves website/package.json exactly once.

Add website/scripts/vercel-ignore-build.sh and configure it as the ignored-build command; compare the current deployment commit with the previous deployed commit from the Git root, restricting the diff to website/.

Test the ignore script: return 0 for firmware-only changes; return 1 for website additions, modifications, deletions and renames, first deployment, missing commits, comparison errors and explicit forced builds; include a website change followed by a firmware-only commit.

Create a preview deployment of the exact accepted revision and run the production-browser smoke suite there, including metadata, assets, 404, all presentation states, delayed 3D loading, rotation, screen mapping and WebGL fallback.
Supervisor: promote or deploy the accepted revision to production only after preview checks pass; verify the ready production deployment and alias https://m5-guardian.vercel.app.

Verify production HTTP responses and browser behavior: correct document title and canonical URL, working GitHub links, successful favicon/social/model/image requests, usable mobile navigation, no pre-activation 3D requests, and functional rotation and fallback.

Confirm the firmware-only case is skipped by the configured ignored-build mechanism and document that Vercel records it as a canceled deployment; record the project settings, accepted revision, deployment identity and rollback procedure without credentials.
Supervisor: mark W06 accepted only after live evidence is reviewed; preserve all firmware work and keep W04 absent from the ledger and shipped site.

CARRY-OVER from the W05 acceptance (supervisor, 2026-11-22): the Lighthouse GATE is measured on the Vercel preview of the exact revision (website/scripts/lighthouse.mjs with LIGHTHOUSE_URL and LIGHTHOUSE_BYPASS = the project's Protection Bypass for Automation secret, never committed or printed). Measured on preview m5-guardian-eqekqsg7n at normal load: median performance 0.96, accessibility 1, best practices 1, LCP 2305 ms, CLS 0, TBT 172 ms; SEO 0.69 only because Vercel sends x-robots-tag: noindex on previews (is-crawlable). W06 must: (1) confirm SEO >= 0.95 on production; (2) make CI run the gate on the preview: a workflow on deployment_status (success, environment Preview) that runs lighthouse.mjs against the deployment URL with the bypass secret from a GitHub Actions secret; the local-server run in website-checks.yml stays informational. Project already created by the supervisor: m5-guardian (flowcoders scope), Root Directory website, Node 24.x, install 'corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile', build 'corepack pnpm run build' (Vercel's own pnpm could not read the pnpm 12 lockfile); root .vercelignore uploads only website/ on CLI deploys.

description: Install page: flash the Guardian onto your own StickS3 from the browser (like the owner's Doutor VPD site), with a first install that offers a backup of the current firmware, an update that keeps settings, signed releases and honest errors.
steps: OWNER (2026-11-22/23): visitors may flash the official image from this website onto their own device, personal and non-commercial; updates are re-flashes from this page; 3D and art rules unchanged. Spike: firmware/evidence/sticks3-W07-flash-spike-20261123.log (MEASURED: update 24.9 s with settings kept, clean install 40.8 s, 8 MB backup 60.8 s, reset via a fresh-connection RTS pulse with DTR low). Requires G26's first GitHub Release to exist for the live check; build and test against fixtures until then.

Port the owner's Doutor VPD flasher core (MIT, attribute in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md): esptool-js 0.7.0 pinned, Web Serial requestPort filtered to Espressif 0x303a, ESP32-S3 check, 460800 baud, writeFlash of the four parts at their offsets (dio, 80m, 8MB, compress), MD5 verify (spark-md5), byte-weighted progress, the fresh-connection reset sequence, friendly English errors (port in use, picker closed, MD5 mismatch, download-mode steps for the StickS3).
Protected ranges for 'Update': never write nvs 0x9000-0xEFFF, phy_init 0xF000 or nvs_cred 0x12000-0x15FFF; refuse any plan that would; 'First install' erases the chip after a double confirm.

Backup first: on 'First install' offer 'Download a backup of what is on the stick now' (esptool-js readFlash 8 MB, ~61 s measured) saved by the browser as a .bin with its sha256 shown; say plainly it can be restored with the same page later ('Restore a backup' writes it back whole, double confirm).

Signed releases: server routes /api/firmware/latest and /api/firmware/[tag]/[file] proxy the GitHub Release (no CORS there), verify the ECDSA P-256 manifest signature with the committed public key and each part's sha256, allow only the four expected parts at their offsets, redirects only to GitHub hosts; the browser re-checks sha256 before writing.

Page /install linked from the hero and the footer: Chrome or Edge on a desktop only (clear message elsewhere, https only); steps with the cable, the download-mode hint, progress, and 'done' text explaining first boot (welcome pages, pick your network); analytics per step with no device data.

LICENSE: firmware/art/LICENSE and website/public/images/LICENSE gain the owner's grant: flashing the official image from this website onto your own device for personal, non-commercial use is permitted; everything else stays reserved.

Tests: unit tests for the plan checks, protected ranges, manifest parsing and signature, error mapping and reset sequence with a fake port and signed fixtures (a throwaway key); the route tests with a mocked fetch. Owner-run real-stick smoke (Playwright + Chrome, not in CI): backup, first install from a non-Guardian image, update keeps settings, restore the backup byte-exact.
Gates: make website-check, the browser suite, the preview Lighthouse gate (the flasher loads esptool-js only after a click), public_check 0. No commit, push or deploy by the worker.

description: Technical SEO and analytics fixes from the 2026-11-24 audit: correct share cards on /install, structured data, favicons, sitemap lastmod, a clearer home meta description, site-wide cookieless analytics, and a Content-Security-Policy.
steps: AUDIT (MEASURED 2026-11-24 on the live site): /install has no og:image and its twitter:title/description are the home page's (app/install/page.tsx:17 sets openGraph, which replaces the root object; twitter is not overridden); no JSON-LD on either page; /favicon.ico is 404 (only app/icon.svg); sitemap has changefreq/priority but no lastmod; the home meta description ends 'This website is a simulation.'; Vercel Web Analytics (enabled on the Pro team) is mounted on /install only; no Content-Security-Policy header. Lighthouse on the preview today: perf 0.96, a11y 1, best practices 1, SEO 1: keep these.

/install share card: its own Open Graph image (app/install/opengraph-image.tsx in the site's existing style, real text only, no new art) and twitter title, description and image matching the install page. Test: an e2e check per page that og:image and twitter:image resolve with 200 and image/png, and that each page's twitter:title equals its own title.

Structured data: JSON-LD in the root layout with schema.org WebSite (name, url) and SoftwareApplication (name 'M5 Guardian', applicationCategory 'SecurityApplication', operatingSystem 'ESP32-S3 firmware (M5Stack StickS3)', license MIT URL, codeRepository / sameAs the GitHub repo, isAccessibleForFree true, offers price 0, softwareVersion = the version in release/version.txt read at build time, downloadUrl /install). No ratings, reviews or invented values. Test: parses as JSON, required keys present, version equals release/version.txt.

Icons: favicon.ico (16/32/48) and apple-icon.png (180) generated from app/icon.svg by a committed script, so the site has no 404 for /favicon.ico. Sitemap: add lastModified from the last commit date of each page's source (build time), keep both URLs. Tests for both.

Home meta description: same length class (<= 160 chars), drop 'This website is a simulation.' from the description only (keep the on-page simulation labels the claims gate requires); e.g. '... five rated faces for advertised settings, and red or amber alerts. Open source, installs from your browser.' Every claim in it must already be in website/claims.json; update claims and tests together.

Analytics: mount Vercel Analytics in the root layout (Vercel builds only, as now), remove the /install-only mount, keep the guardian_install custom event payload unchanged (action, result only, no device data). Update the page text that describes analytics if it says install page only. Test: the e2e that checks no analytics script in a non-Vercel build still passes; the payload test still passes.

Content-Security-Policy in next.config (headers): first as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only on a preview, list what it would block (Next inline bootstrap, esptool-js and spark-md5 dynamic imports, Vercel Analytics script and its /_vercel/insights endpoint, the /api/firmware routes, data:/blob: for the backup download), then enforce with exactly those sources (nonce or hash for inline if Next requires it). The install flow must still work under the enforced policy in the browser suite (mocked Web Serial as in W07). Record the final policy and why each source is there in website/DEPLOYMENT.md.

Gates (same as W07): make website-check green (unit tests first, red logs kept), the Playwright browser suite including axe and the 320/768/1440 px overflow checks, tools/public_check.py --require-map with 0 findings, and the preview Lighthouse gate on GitHub (website-preview-lighthouse.yml: performance >= 0.9, accessibility 1, SEO >= 0.95, LCP <= 2.5 s, CLS <= 0.1, TBT <= 200 ms). Never commit, push or deploy; hand off with READY FOR REVIEW.
Live check after deploy (reviewer): curl / and /install show og:image + matching twitter tags, JSON-LD present, /favicon.ico 200, CSP header present, Analytics script on /.

description: Content page /what-it-detects that answers the searches people make (deauth detector, evil twin detector, is my Wi-Fi WPA3, M5StickS3 firmware), every statement held to the claims gate.
steps: AUDIT (MEASURED 2026-11-24): a web search for the project returns nothing from the site; the niche searches return Periscope-OS (Hackster), Bruce, M5Stick-Nemo, Spacehuhn DeauthDetector and DSTIKE's deauth detector. The home page (~790 words) and /install (~470) do not answer 'can the StickS3 detect deauth / evil twin attacks', 'how do I check my Wi-Fi uses WPA3', or 'what firmware turns an M5StickS3 into a Wi-Fi monitor'.

Page /what-it-detects: short sections, each a plain question as an H2 with a direct first-sentence answer: what the Guardian rates (the five faces and the advertised settings they come from), what makes it red (disconnect bursts, another BSSID using your network's name, network-pattern alerts), what makes it amber (nearby activity, router changes and the ROUTER CHANGES setting), what it does not do (receive-only: it never transmits attacks, never joins other networks, cannot see inside encrypted traffic), and how it compares to transmit-capable multi-tool firmwares (no names of other projects needed; describe the category). Wording rule: radio events by counts, scope and alert colour only.

Every factual sentence is a website/claims.json entry with a verbatim source quote (README, firmware README, docs/attack-coverage.md); lib/claims.test.ts must pass. No invented numbers. Title <= 60 chars and a meta description <= 160 chars written for these searches, own Open Graph image in the W08 style, canonical, in the sitemap, linked from the home page (a visible link near the alert section) and the footer.
Structured data: none beyond the W08 site-wide JSON-LD (Google limits FAQ rich results to government and health sites, so no FAQPage markup).

Gates (same as W07): make website-check green (unit tests first, red logs kept), the Playwright browser suite including axe and the 320/768/1440 px overflow checks, tools/public_check.py --require-map with 0 findings, and the preview Lighthouse gate on GitHub (website-preview-lighthouse.yml: performance >= 0.9, accessibility 1, SEO >= 0.95, LCP <= 2.5 s, CLS <= 0.1, TBT <= 200 ms). Never commit, push or deploy; hand off with READY FOR REVIEW.
Live check after deploy (reviewer): the page is 200, in sitemap.xml, linked from / and the footer, Lighthouse gate green on its preview URL too (add the page to the gate's URL list).
